coverage.impact_of_missing: Spread/premium-discount/tracking-error going to null does not block the structure gate (only the four structural booleans are hard-required and all are confirmed false here); it does lower the tradability data's completeness. Given AUM (USD 4.2B-42.5B) and avg daily volume (3.4M-32.4M shares) are all comfortably above the run's US thresholds (min AUM USD 100M, min trading value USD 5M/day), true spreads are very likely tight for all three, but that is inference, not a verified figure, so it is left null rather than estimated.

candidates.name: Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund
candidates.index: Energy Select Sector Index (S&P 500 energy constituents: oil, gas & consumable fuels; energy equipment & services)
candidates.notes: The standard broad benchmark for the GICS Energy (oil & gas) sector; role in this comparison is the sector's broad index. Note it is also fairly concentrated — Exxon Mobil (19.9%) + Chevron (15.2%) = ~35.1% of the fund across only 21 holdings, so 'broad' does not mean flat-weighted; flagged as a mega-cap tilt worth naming alongside the 'broad index' label.

structure_trading.real_cost_notes: Physical/sampled replication (not swap-based), 0.08% expense ratio is among the lowest in the sector-ETF category; USD 42.5B AUM and ~32.4M shares/day average volume imply very high liquidity and (inferred, not measured) tight spreads.

candidates.name: Utilities Select Sector SPDR Fund
candidates.index: Utilities Select Sector Index (S&P 500 utilities constituents: electric, multi, gas utilities, independent power & renewable producers)
candidates.notes: Represents the electric-power side of the sector (this sector spans both oil & gas and electric power) — top holdings include NextEra Energy (13.1%), Southern Co (7.5%), Duke Energy (7.1%), Constellation Energy (6.8%), American Electric Power (5.1%). Moderately concentrated in a handful of large regulated/independent power utilities rather than flat across all 31 names, distinct in construction from XLE's oil & gas mega-caps and from XOP's equal-weight sub-industry approach.

structure_trading.real_cost_notes: Physical/sampled replication, 0.08% expense ratio; USD 22.4B AUM and ~20.4M shares/day average volume imply very high liquidity and (inferred, not measured) tight spreads.

candidates.name: SPDR S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production ETF
candidates.index: S&P Oil & Gas Exploration & Production Select Industry Index (modified equal-weight)
candidates.notes: The structurally different candidate: a modified equal-weighted sub-industry play (Integrated Oil & Gas, Oil & Gas E&P, Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing) rather than a cap-weighted broad sector fund. Top holding is only 3.9% (PBF Energy) across 51 names, deliberately spreading exposure across large/mid/small-cap E&P and refining names instead of concentrating in supermajors — the opposite construction from XLE. Higher expense ratio (0.35% vs 0.08%) and smaller AUM/volume than XLE/XLU, though still above the run's US structure-gate thresholds.

structure_trading.real_cost_notes: Physical/sampled replication of a modified equal-weight index; higher expense ratio (0.35%) and more frequent rebalancing turnover to maintain equal weighting than a cap-weighted sector fund, which is a real cost beyond the headline ratio. USD 4.16B AUM and ~3.37M shares/day average volume are smaller than XLE/XLU but still well above the run's US thresholds (min AUM USD 100M, min trading value USD 5M/day).
